notes: All four Engineering Services Examination (ESE) branch papers were researched on 2026-11-17 from the official ESE 2027 Examination Notice No. 02/2027-ENGG (notification date 16.09.2026, preliminary examination 31.01.2027, main examination 18.06.2027). The syllabus text was extracted from the full 62-page notification PDF as mirrored by madeeasy.in (a reputable ESE coaching institute); the PDF itself is the official UPSC notice (its first page cites 'The Commission's website - https://upsc.gov.in').

The official location of the notice on upsc.gov.in (the 'Exam Notification: Engineering Services (Preliminary) Examination, 2027' item) is listed per exam: the item's URL was taken from the fetched upsc.gov.in homepage (no URL invented), but the deep Drupal page itself returned 504/Akamai 'Access Denied' for both curl and headless browser from this sandbox, which is why the madeeasy mirror of the PDF is the primary fetched source. The upsc.gov.in homepage itself WAS fetched successfully and its What's New listing verified the notice's existence and title.

Per the notification, each branch's syllabus is stated as 'Contents for syllabi of both the Papers together for Preliminary Examination/Stage-I (objective type Paper-II) and separately for Main/Stage-II Examination (Conventional type Paper-I and Paper-II)' — i.e. the same topic lists serve both Stage-I Paper-II and the Stage-II Paper-I/Paper-II. Topics are numbered 1-6 within each of the two papers; each paper's numbered topics are recorded verbatim as the topic line, with additional 'topic — sub-area' lines that condense the notification's own sub-bullets (e.g. the (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) sub-parts of Civil Environmental Engineering) at clause level.

The common General Studies and Engineering Aptitude paper (Stage-I Paper-I, common to all candidates) was trivially in the same fetched PDF, so its 10 stated topic lines are included as a fifth entry, as sanctioned; nothing was chased beyond the notification.

Mechanical Engineering Paper-II topic 1 'Engineering Mechanics' covers strength-of-materials content (stresses and strains, bending moment and shear force diagrams, bending, slope and deflection, torsion, thin and thick cylinders) exactly as the notification states it.
Electronics paper is titled 'Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering' (Category-IV) in the notification; the exam id 'ese-electronics' follows the task list.

topics: Paper-I: Building Materials

Paper-I: Building Materials — stone, lime, glass, plastics, steel, FRP, ceramics, aluminium, fly ash, basic admixtures, timber, bricks and aggregates: classification, properties and selection criteria

Paper-I: Building Materials — cement: types, composition, properties, uses, specifications and various tests; lime and cement mortars and concrete: properties and tests; design of concrete mixes: proportioning of aggregates and methods of mix design

Paper-I: Solid Mechanics — elastic constants, stress, plane stress, strains, plane strain, Mohr's circle of stress and strain, elastic theories of failure, principal stresses, bending, shear and torsion
Paper-I: Structural Analysis
Paper-I: Structural Analysis — basics of strength of materials; analysis of determinate and indeterminate structures; trusses, beams, plane frames
Paper-I: Structural Analysis — rolling loads, influence lines, unit load method and other methods
Paper-I: Structural Analysis — free and forced vibrations of single- and multi-degree-freedom systems; suspended cables; concepts and use of computer aided design

Paper-I: Design of Steel Structures — working stress methods; design of tension and compression members, beams and beam-column connections, built-up sections, girders, industrial roofs; principles of ultimate load design
Paper-I: Design of Concrete and Masonry Structures

Paper-I: Design of Concrete and Masonry Structures — limit state design for bending, shear, axial compression and combined forces; design of beams, slabs, lintels, foundations, retaining walls, tanks, staircases
Paper-I: Design of Concrete and Masonry Structures — principles of prestressed concrete design including materials and methods; earthquake resistant design of structures; design of masonry structure

Paper-I: Construction Practice, Planning and Management — construction planning, equipment, site investigation and management including estimation with latest project management tools and network analysis; analysis of rates; tendering process and contract management; quality control, productivity, operation cost; land acquisition; labour safety and welfare
Paper-II: Flow of Fluids, Hydraulic Machines and Hydro Power

Paper-II: Fluid Mechanics, Open Channel Flow, Pipe Flow — fluid properties; dimensional analysis and modelling; fluid dynamics including flow kinematics and measurements; flow net; viscosity; boundary layer and control, drag, lift; principles in open channel flow, flow controls; hydraulic jump; surges; pipe networks

Paper-II: Hydraulic Machines and Hydro Power — various pumps, air vessels, hydraulic turbines: types, classifications and performance parameters; power house: classification and layout, storage, pondage, control of supply
Paper-II: Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering

Paper-II: Hydrology — hydrological cycle, ground water hydrology, well hydrology and related data analysis; streams and their gauging; river morphology; flood, drought and their management; capacity of reservoirs

Paper-II: Water Resources Engineering — multipurpose uses of water; river basins and their potential; irrigation systems, water demand assessment; resources, storages and their yields; water logging, canal and drainage design

Paper-II: Water Resources Engineering — gravity dams, falls, weirs, energy dissipaters, barrage distribution works, cross drainage works and head-works and their design; concepts in canal design, construction and maintenance; river training; measurement and analysis of rainfall

Paper-II: Environmental Engineering — Water Supply Engineering (sources, estimation, quality standards and testing of water and their treatment; water demand; drinking water standards; water treatment plants; water distribution networks)

Paper-II: Environmental Engineering — Waste Water Engineering (planning and design of domestic waste water, sewage collection and disposal; plumbing systems; sewerage systems; sludge management, treatment, disposal and re-use; industrial waste waters and effluent treatment plants)
Paper-II: Environmental Engineering — Solid Waste Management (sources and classification of solid wastes, planning and design of its management system, disposal systems, beneficial aspects of wastes)
Paper-II: Environmental Engineering — Air, Noise pollution and Ecology: concepts and general methodology
Paper-II: Geo-technical Engineering and Foundation Engineering

Paper-II: Geo-technical Engineering — soil exploration: planning and methods; properties of soil, classification, various tests and inter-relationships; permeability and seepage; compressibility, consolidation and shearing resistance; earth pressure theories and stress distribution in soil; properties and uses of geo-synthetics

Paper-II: Foundation Engineering — types of foundations and selection criteria; bearing capacity, settlement analysis; design and testing of shallow and deep foundations; slope stability analysis; earthen embankments, dams and earth retaining structures: types, analysis and design; principles of ground modifications
Paper-II: Surveying and Geology

Paper-II: Surveying — classification of surveys, various methodologies, instruments and analysis of measurement of distances, elevation and directions; field astronomy, global positioning system; map preparation; photogrammetry; remote sensing concepts; survey layout for culverts, canals, bridges, road/railway alignment and buildings; setting out of curves
Paper-II: Geology — basic knowledge of engineering geology and its application in projects
Paper-II: Transportation Engineering
Paper-II: Transportation — highways: planning and construction methodology, alignment and geometric design; traffic surveys and controls; principles of flexible and rigid pavement design
Paper-II: Transportation — tunneling: alignment, methods of construction, disposal of muck, drainage, lighting and ventilation

Paper-II: Transportation — railways systems: terminology, planning, designs and maintenance practices, track modernization; harbours: terminology, layouts and planning; airports: layout, planning and design

topics: Paper-I: Fluid Mechanics
Paper-I: Fluid Mechanics — basic concepts and properties of fluids, manometry, fluid statics, buoyancy, equations of motion, Bernoulli's equation and applications
Paper-I: Fluid Mechanics — viscous flow of incompressible fluids, laminar and turbulent flows, flow through pipes and head losses in pipes
Paper-I: Thermodynamics and Heat transfer

Paper-I: Thermodynamics — thermodynamic systems and processes; properties of pure substance; zeroth, first and second laws; entropy, irreversibility and availability; analysis of thermodynamic cycles: Rankine, Otto, Diesel and Dual cycles; ideal and real gases, compressibility factor, gas mixtures

Paper-I: Heat transfer — modes of heat transfer; steady and unsteady heat conduction; thermal resistance, fins; free and forced convection, correlations; radiative heat transfer; boiling and condensation; heat exchanger performance analysis
Paper-I: IC Engines, Refrigeration and Air conditioning
Paper-I: IC Engines — SI and CI engines, engine systems and components, performance characteristics and testing; fuels; emissions and emission control

Paper-I: Refrigeration and Air conditioning — vapour compression refrigeration, refrigerants and working cycles, compressors, condensers, evaporators and expansion devices; other refrigeration systems (vapour absorption, vapour jet, thermo-electric, vortex tube); psychrometric properties and processes, comfort chart, comfort and industrial air conditioning, load calculations and heat pumps

Paper-I: Turbo Machinery — reciprocating and rotary pumps; Pelton wheel, Kaplan and Francis turbines, velocity diagrams, impulse and reaction principles; steam and gas turbines; theory of jet propulsion — pulse jet and ram jet engines; reciprocating and rotary compressors: theory and applications

Paper-I: Power Plant Engineering — Rankine and Brayton cycles with regeneration and reheat; fuels and their properties, flue gas analysis; boilers; steam turbines; condensers, air ejectors, electrostatic precipitators and cooling towers: theory, design, types and applications

Paper-I: Renewable Sources of Energy — solar radiation; solar thermal energy collection (flat plate and focusing collectors), solar thermal energy storage; applications: heating, cooling and power generation; solar photovoltaic conversion; harnessing of wind energy; bio-mass and tidal energy; working principles of fuel cells
Paper-II: Engineering Mechanics

Paper-II: Engineering Mechanics — analysis of system of forces, friction, centroid and centre of gravity, dynamics; stresses and strains, compound stresses and strains, bending moment and shear force diagrams; theory of bending stresses, slope and deflection, torsion; thin and thick cylinders, spheres

Paper-II: Engineering Materials — basic crystallography, alloys and phase diagrams, heat treatment; ferrous and non-ferrous metals; non-metallic materials; basics of nano-materials; mechanical properties and testing; corrosion prevention and control
Paper-II: Mechanisms and Machines

Paper-II: Mechanisms — types of kinematic pair, mobility, inversions, kinematic analysis; velocity and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms; cams with uniform acceleration and retardation, cycloidal motion, oscillating followers

Paper-II: Machines — vibrations: free and forced vibration of undamped and damped SDOF systems, transmissibility ratio, vibration isolation, critical speed of shafts; gears: geometry of tooth profiles, law of gearing, involute profile, interference, helical, spiral and worm gears; gear trains: simple, compound and epicyclic

Paper-II: Machines — dynamic analysis: slider-crank mechanisms, turning moment computations, balancing of revolving and reciprocating masses; gyroscopes: effect of gyroscopic couple on automobiles, ships and aircrafts; governors

Paper-II: Design of Machine Elements — design for static and dynamic loading; failure theories; fatigue strength and the S-N diagram; principles of design of machine elements such as riveted, welded and bolted joints, shafts, spur gears, rolling and sliding contact bearings, brakes and clutches, flywheels
Paper-II: Manufacturing, Industrial and Maintenance Engineering

Paper-II: Manufacturing — metal casting, metal forming, metal joining; machining and machine tool operations; limits, fits and tolerances; metrology and inspection; computer integrated manufacturing, FMS
Paper-II: Industrial — production planning and control; inventory control and operations research: CPM-PERT

Paper-II: Maintenance — failure concepts and characteristics, reliability, failure analysis; machine vibration, data acquisition, fault detection, vibration monitoring; field balancing of rotors; noise monitoring; wear and debris analysis; signature analysis; NDT techniques in condition monitoring
Paper-II: Mechatronics and Robotics

Paper-II: Mechatronics — microprocessors and microcontrollers: architecture, programming, I/O, computer interfacing; programmable logic controller; sensors and actuators (piezoelectric accelerometer, Hall effect sensor, optical encoder, resolver, inductosyn, pneumatic and hydraulic actuators, stepper motor); control systems: mathematical modelling of physical systems, control signals, controllability and observability
Paper-II: Robotics — robot classification, robot specification, notation; direct and inverse kinematics; homogeneous coordinates and arm equation of four-axis SCARA robot

topics: Paper-I: Engineering Mathematics — matrix theory, eigen values and eigen vectors; numerical methods for solution of non-linear algebraic equations and differential equations; Fourier series; linear, non-linear and partial differential equations; complex variables; probability and statistics fundamentals, sampling theorem, random variables, normal and Poisson distributions, correlation and regression analysis

Paper-I: Electrical Materials — electrical engineering materials, crystal structures and defects, ceramic materials, insulating materials; magnetic materials: basics, properties and applications; ferrites, ferro-magnetic materials and components; basics of solid state physics, conductors; photo-conductivity; basics of nano materials and superconductors
Paper-I: Electric Circuits and Fields

Paper-I: Electric Circuits — circuit elements, network graph, KCL, KVL, node and mesh analysis; ideal current and voltage sources; Thevenin's, Norton's, superposition and maximum power transfer theorems; transient response of DC and AC networks; sinusoidal steady state analysis; basic filter concepts; two-port networks; three phase circuits; magnetically coupled circuits

Paper-I: Electric Fields — Gauss theorem; electric field and potential due to point, line, plane and spherical charge distributions; Ampere's and Biot-Savart's laws; inductance, dielectrics, capacitance; Maxwell's equations

Paper-I: Electrical and Electronic Measurements — principles of measurement, accuracy, precision and standards; bridges and potentiometers; moving coil, moving iron, dynamometer and induction type instruments; measurement of voltage, current, power, energy and power factor; instrument transformers; digital voltmeters and multimeters; phase, time and frequency measurement; Q-meters; oscilloscopes; potentiometric recorders; error analysis; basics of sensors and transducers; data acquisition systems

Paper-I: Computer Fundamentals — number systems, Boolean algebra, arithmetic functions; basic architecture, central processing unit, I/O and memory organisation; peripheral devices; data representation and programming; basics of operating system and networking; virtual memory, file systems; elements of programming languages

Paper-I: Basic Electronics Engineering — basics of semiconductor diodes and transistors and characteristics; junction and field effect transistors (BJT, FET and MOSFETs); different types of transistor amplifiers, equivalent circuits and frequency response; oscillators and other circuits; feedback amplifiers
Paper-II: Analog and Digital Electronics

Paper-II: Analog electronics — operational amplifiers: characteristics and applications; sample and hold circuits; A/D and D/A converters; basics of filter circuits and applications, simple active filters; microprocessor basics: interfaces and applications; basics of linear integrated circuits
Paper-II: Digital electronics — combinational and sequential logic circuits; multiplexers; multivibrators

Paper-II: Communication basics (within Analog and Digital Electronics) — analog communication basics, modulation and de-modulation, noise and bandwidth, transmitters and receivers, signal to noise ratio; digital communication basics: sampling, quantizing, coding, frequency and time domain multiplexing; power line carrier communication systems

Paper-II: Systems and Signal Processing — representation of continuous and discrete-time signals, shifting and scaling operations; linear, time-invariant and causal systems; Fourier series representation of continuous periodic signals; sampling theorem; Fourier and Laplace transforms, Z transforms, discrete Fourier transform, FFT; linear convolution; discrete cosine transform; FIR filter, IIR filter, bilinear transformation

Paper-II: Control Systems — principles of feedback; transfer function, block diagrams and signal flow graphs; steady-state errors; Routh-Hurwitz criterion, Nyquist techniques, Bode plots, root loci; lag, lead and lead-lag compensation; stability analysis, transient and frequency response analysis; state space model, state transition matrix, controllability and observability; linear state variable feedback; PID and industrial controllers
Paper-II: Electrical Machines
Paper-II: Electrical Machines — transformers: single phase and three phase connections, parallel operation, auto-transformer; energy conversion principles
Paper-II: Electrical Machines — DC machines: types, windings, generator characteristics, armature reaction and commutation, starting and speed control of motors

Paper-II: Electrical Machines — induction motors: principles, types, performance characteristics, starting and speed control; synchronous machines: performance, regulation, parallel operation of generators, motor starting, characteristics and applications; servo and stepper motors
Paper-II: Power Systems

Paper-II: Power Systems — basic power generation concepts; steam, gas and water turbines; transmission line models and performance; cable performance; insulation, corona and radio interference; power factor correction

Paper-II: Power Systems — symmetrical components, fault analysis, principles of protection systems, basics of solid state relays and digital protection; circuit breakers; radial and ring-main distribution systems

Paper-II: Power Systems — matrix representation of power systems, load flow analysis, voltage control and economic operation; system stability concepts, swing curves and equal area criterion; HVDC transmission and FACTS concepts; concepts of power system dynamics; distributed generation, solar and wind power, smart grid concepts; environmental implications; fundamentals of power economics
Paper-II: Power Electronics and Drives

Paper-II: Power Electronics — semiconductor power diodes, transistors, thyristors, triacs, GTOs, MOSFETs and IGBTs: static characteristics and principles of operation; triggering circuits; phase control rectifiers; bridge converters: fully controlled and half controlled; principles of choppers and inverters

Paper-II: Drives — basic concepts of adjustable speed DC and AC drives; DC-DC switched mode converters; DC-AC switched mode converters; resonant converters; high frequency inductors and transformers; power supplies

topics: Paper-I: Basic Electronics Engineering

Paper-I: Basic Electronics Engineering — basics of semiconductors; diode/transistor basics and characteristics; diodes for different uses; junction and field effect transistors (BJTs, JFETs, MOSFETs); transistor amplifiers of different types, oscillators and other circuits; basics of integrated circuits (ICs): bipolar, MOS and CMOS ICs; basics of linear ICs, operational amplifiers and their applications (linear/non-linear); optical sources/detectors; basics of opto-electronics and its applications

Paper-I: Basic Electrical Engineering — DC circuits: Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws, mesh and nodal analysis, circuit theorems; electromagnetism, Faraday's and Lenz's laws, induced EMF and its uses; single-phase AC circuits; transformers, efficiency; basics of DC machines, induction machines and synchronous machines; electrical power sources: hydroelectric, thermal, nuclear, wind, solar; basics of batteries and their uses

Paper-I: Materials Science — electrical engineering materials; crystal structure and defects; ceramic materials: structures, composites, processing and uses; insulating laminates for electronics; magnetic materials: basics, classification, ferrites, ferro/para-magnetic materials and components; nano materials: basics, preparation, purification, sintering, nano particles and uses; nano-optical/magnetic/electronic materials; superconductivity and uses

Paper-I: Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation — principles of measurement, accuracy, precision and standards; analog and digital systems for measurement; static/dynamic characteristics of measurement systems, errors, statistical analysis and curve fitting; measurement systems for non-electrical quantities; basics of telemetry; different types of transducers and displays; data acquisition system basics

Paper-I: Network Theory — network graphs and matrices; wye-delta transformation; linear constant coefficient differential equations: time domain analysis of RLC circuits; solution of network equations using Laplace transforms: frequency domain analysis of RLC circuits; two-port network parameters, driving point and transfer functions; state equations for networks; steady state sinusoidal analysis
Paper-I: Analog and Digital Circuits

Paper-I: Analog circuits — small signal equivalent circuits of diodes, BJTs and FETs; biasing and stability of BJT and JFET amplifier circuits; analysis/design of amplifiers (single/multi-stage); feedback and uses; active filters, timers, multipliers, wave shaping; A/D and D/A converters

Paper-I: Digital circuits — Boolean algebra and uses; logic gates, digital IC families; combinational and sequential circuits; basics of multiplexers, counters/registers/memories/microprocessors: design and applications
Paper-II: Analog and Digital Communication Systems

Paper-II: Analog and digital communication — random signals, noise, probability theory, information theory; analog versus digital communication and applications; AM, FM systems, transmitters/receivers, theory/practice/standards, SNR comparison

Paper-II: Digital communication basics — sampling, quantizing, coding; PCM, DPCM, multiplexing (audio/video); digital modulation: ASK, FSK, PSK; multiple access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA; optical communication: fibre optics, theory, practice/standards

Paper-II: Control Systems — classification of signals and systems; application of signal and system theory; system realisation; transforms and their applications; signal flow graphs, Routh-Hurwitz criteria, root loci, Nyquist/Bode plots; feedback systems: open and closed loop types, stability analysis, steady state, transient and frequency response analysis; design of control systems, compensators, elements of lead/lag compensation, PID and industrial controllers
Paper-II: Computer Organization and Architecture

Paper-II: Computer organization — basic architecture, CPU, I/O organisation, memory organisation, peripheral devices, trends; hardware/software issues; data representation and programming; operating systems: basics, processes, characteristics, applications; memory management, virtual memory, file systems, protection and security
Paper-II: Databases and languages — data bases: different types, characteristics and design; transactions and concurrency control; elements of programming languages, typical examples
Paper-II: Electro Magnetics — elements of vector calculus, Maxwell's equations: basic concepts; Gauss' and Stokes' theorems; wave propagation through different media
Paper-II: Transmission lines — different types, basics, Smith's chart, impedance matching/transformation, S-parameters, pulse excitation, uses
Paper-II: Waveguides — basics, rectangular types, modes, cut-off frequency, dispersion, dielectric types
Paper-II: Antennas — radiation pattern, monopoles/dipoles, gain, arrays: active/passive, theory, uses
Paper-II: Advanced Electronics Topics
Paper-II: VLSI technology — processing, lithography, interconnects, packaging, testing
Paper-II: VLSI design — principles, MUX/ROM/PLA-based design, Moore and Mealy circuit design; pipeline concepts and functions; design for testability, examples
Paper-II: DSP — discrete time signals and systems, uses; digital filters: FIR/IIR types, design; speech/audio/radar signal processing uses
Paper-II: Microprocessors and microcontrollers — basics, interrupts, DMA, instruction sets, interfacing; controllers and uses; embedded systems
Paper-II: Advanced Communication Topics
Paper-II: Communication networks — principles/practices/technologies/uses; OSI model/security; basic packet multiplexed streams/scheduling; cellular networks: types, analysis; protocols (TCP/TCPIP)
Paper-II: Microwave and satellite communication — terrestrial/space type LOS systems, block schematics, link calculations, system design
Paper-II: Communication satellites — orbits, characteristics, systems, uses; fibre-optic communication systems: block schematics, link calculations, system design
